key_insight: Monitoring intermediate answer confidence during chain-of-thought reveals predictable dynamics: correct reasoning trajectories typically attain a high-confidence stable point early, enabling reliable early stopping to save compute and avoid overthinking.
problem_solved: Deciding when a large reasoning model should stop generating chains-of-thought so as to minimize inference cost and prevent accuracy degradation from overthinking.
method: Track per-step answer confidence scores (e.g., softmax probabilities or calibrated scores) throughout chain-of-thought generation.
Characterize confidence dynamics (peaks, plateaus, declines, variance) and derive simple heuristic or learned stopping rules that detect an 'early high-confidence' stable point.
Apply the stopping criterion at inference to terminate reasoning early and output the current answer; evaluate trade-offs between accuracy and compute across benchmarks.
impact: Makes long-chain-of-thought reasoning more efficient and robust—substantially reducing inference cost while often improving final accuracy by avoiding late-stage overthinking. Practical for deploying large reasoning models in resource-constrained or latency-sensitive settings.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram: chain-of-thought steps with an overlaid confidence curve, highlighting the early high-confidence plateau and stop point.
Decision boundary graphic: confidence dynamics patterns (correct vs incorrect) with the early-stopping threshold illustrated.
Bar/line chart: compute cost (tokens or time) vs accuracy comparing full reasoning vs early-stopped runs.
Flowchart: simple runtime loop showing confidence monitoring, stop/continue decision, and final-answer extraction.
paper_title: Early Stopping for Large Reasoning Models via Confidence Dynamics
paper_authors: Parsa Hosseini, Sumit Nawathe, Mahdi Salmani, Meisam Razaviyayn, Soheil Feizi
